messages.author: f53f4ca2c430170d
messages.subject: Shinystan scaling
parts:
Hey, I basically don't use shinystan because my models are too big (I'm just not going to wait for an hour while everything loads) but... doesn't shinystan rely on a dplyr-based backend for manipulations? I've used both the postgres and the sqlite backends for data before with dplyr and they seem to work really well but I'm not sure how well they would mesh with the ShinyStan design.

If you have tens of thousands of parameters, you could make something like ShinyStan work well by keeping a tight leash on a "window" (maybe grep-defined) of which parameters to consider at any one time. Is ShinyStan at this point really built around a load-everything-plot-everything strategy or would it be possible to have it always load only a limited set (which could be changed in the interface, but limited to X parameters.

Krzysztof

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Re: Shinystan scaling
parts: It's basically a load everything plot everything setup at the moment, but I agree that's not ideal. It doesn't actually use dplyr at all, although I'm not opposed to it. It was suggested to me when I was initially working on ShinyStan that avoiding dplyr entirely would be preferable because of dependency issues. But perhaps being able to use different backends with dplyr would be helpful. In general there's a lot of room for improvement in the way ShinyStan handles large models (well, all models I guess).
